title: activity
description: Activity definition schema — unified ordered, kind-tagged steps[] (technique | action | checkpoint | loop).

items.description: Qualified snake_case noun phrase (>=2 words, AP-60), or an enumerated bare-word exemption.

reads.description: Session variables this activity consults: gate and routing conditions, loop collections, prose interpolations, and the bound operations' own inputs it does not supply itself. A name written by an earlier step of the same activity is resolved internally and is not declared here.

type.description: Declared type. The server validates checkpoint setVariable values against it, warn-only: a mismatch is stored as written and surfaced in _meta.validation and on the variable_set history event. Agents honor it for their own writes.

values.description: The complete set of values a string variable admits. The server validates writes against it warn-only, as it does the declared type.

defaultValue.description: Initial value the server seeds into the session variable bag at session creation (start_session fresh sessions and dispatch_child children), recorded as one variables_seeded history event. Do not gate a defaulted variable with exists/notExists — seeding makes the gate constant (check:variable-model enforces this).

required.description: Authoring metadata; the server does not check that the variable is ever set.

writes.description: Session variables this activity puts into the bag: its bound operations' outputs (under their declared id or the step binding's remap target), its checkpoint setVariable effects and its `set` action targets. Contributed to the including workflow's variable set, defaultValue included — a loop variable is iteration state and is not declared here.

variables.description: The session variables this activity reads and writes. Its writes are declarations contributed to the including workflow's variable set; its reads are the names it needs that workflow to supply.

techniques.description: Activity-wide technique references (`::` paths); bundled into get_activity.

maxChars.description: Per-technique character cap layered on the server-derived per-activity eager-delivery budget: a step technique whose composed wire form exceeds this is not inlined and is fetched with get_technique { step_id }. Set to 0 to opt this activity out of eager step-technique bundling entirely.

bundleTechniques.description: Opt-in hybrid bundling: get_activity inlines each step technique whose composed wire form is at most maxChars and whose gate answers true at activity open; larger ones, and those whose gate has no answer yet, remain lazy-fetched via get_technique. Bundled deliveries are recorded as technique_bundled history events and satisfy the manifest fidelity check.

id.description: Identifier for this step within the activity. Optional: the loader derives it from the last `::` segment of the technique name.

name.description: The `group::operation` (or bare op / `workflow::group::op`) technique reference this step invokes.

inputs.description: Input deviations: op input id → source expression (rename of a bag variable, literal, or `{template}`). Only what differs from same-name binding or a declared default.

outputs.description: Output remaps: op output id → the workflow variable name its produced value lands under, when it differs from the output id.

technique.description: Canonical per-step binding: a `group::operation` reference (string) for a step with no deviations, or `{ name, inputs?, outputs? }` when the step supplies input deviations or output remaps.

action.description: Action verb, interpreted by the executing agent. The server has no action interpreter: executing `set` is the worker's job, and its value reaches the session variable bag when the worker reports it in the `variables_changed` its orchestrator relays on next_activity. `set` is slated for removal at the next workflow-schema major (#166 B7/B12).

description.description: Human-readable description of what this action does

condition.description: Condition that must be true for this action to execute

when.description: Inline boolean expression that gates this step. Operators: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, bare identifier truthiness, unary !, &&, ||, and parentheses. Precedence (C-style, tightest first): () > ! > comparisons > && > ||. Mixing && and || at the same nesting depth requires parentheses. Examples: "has_saved_state == true", "remediation_round > 0", "a == true && b != false", "(a && b) || c", "is_review_mode != true && (problem_complexity == \"moderate\" || problem_complexity == \"complex\")". Evaluated by the executing agent against current variable state; the server never evaluates gates. Mechanical nets (e2e walker, guards) use the shared reference evaluator and treat invalid expressions as false (step does not run). On a checkpoint step, only `condition` (not `when`) enables condition_not_met dismissal.

condition.description: LEGACY: Structured condition that must be true for this step to execute, evaluated by the executing agent. Prefer the `when` inline expression for simple comparisons — except on a checkpoint step, where the `condition` field is what makes the checkpoint dismissible via respond_checkpoint condition_not_met.

required.description: Declared only when false (an optional step). An omitted `required` means the step is required; `required: true` is redundant and rejected (AP-64). A worker hint — the server does not check it.

id.description: Identifier for this step within the activity.

actions.description: Control actions; may be empty for marker steps.

id.description: Identifier for this step within the activity; the stable checkpoint-response replay key.

ref.description: Checkpoint-fragment reference: `[workflow::]name`, resolved against the declaring workflow's `fragments.checkpoints` (bare name: declaring workflow, then meta). Mutually exclusive with the body fields — a ref step carries only its id and, when the fragment declares none, a condition.

message.description: Message presented to the user. Required on an inline checkpoint; forbidden alongside `ref`.

setVariable.description: Variable assignments the server applies to the session variable bag when the option is selected — the one engine-applied checkpoint effect. Values are validated against the declared variable type, warn-only: mismatches are stored as written and surfaced in _meta.validation; `{name}` template passthroughs are exempt.

exit.description: Exit of the owning activity this option selects — a name from the activity's `exits[]`, never an activity id. The destination is the workflow's to state: `present_checkpoint` reads it from the workflow graph so the option's consequence is stated before the user chooses. An adhoc checkpoint has no declared exits, so its options carry setVariable only.

options.description: Decision options with effects. Required on an inline checkpoint; forbidden alongside `ref`.

defaultOption.description: The answer a soft gate takes when no person is reached.

autoAdvanceMs.description: The interval the server spends before applying a soft gate's default on respond_checkpoint { auto_advance: true }.

id.description: Identifier for this step within the activity.

name.description: Structural label for the iteration (the one step kind that carries a name).

over.description: Collection expression iterated by a forEach loop.

breakCondition.description: Early-exit condition, evaluated by the executing agent each iteration.

maxIterations.description: Safety bound on iteration count, enforced by the executing agent.

steps.description: The loop body, a nested ordered list of steps.
Ordered, kind-tagged execution steps for this activity

id.description: Outcome name, unique within the activity. Kebab-case, in the activity's vocabulary — never an activity id.

when.description: Inline boolean expression selecting this exit, evaluated agent-side against the variable bag in the `when` dialect the step gates use. Omitted on an exit only a checkpoint option selects, and on the default exit.

isDefault.description: The outcome when no `when` matched and no checkpoint option selected an exit — including a checkpoint dismissed because its condition was not met. Declared exactly once on an activity with two or more exits; `isDefault: false` is redundant and rejected.

immediate.description: Selecting this exit at a checkpoint ends the step sequence there: the remaining steps do not run and the step-manifest check accounts for them. Declared for the aborts, where the tail would otherwise run against the user's decision. Without it an exit is recorded when chosen and taken when the sequence ends. `immediate: false` is redundant and rejected.

exits.description: Named outcomes of this activity, one of which it takes when its steps end. Each is bound to a destination in the workflow's `graph`; an unbound exit fails the workflow load. Omitted on an activity that is terminal by omission.

workflow.description: ID of the workflow to trigger

description.description: Description of when/why this workflow is triggered

passContext.description: Context variable names the dispatching agent relays to the child workflow. The server does not copy them — a child session's bag starts from the child workflow's own declared defaults, nothing more.

triggers.description: Workflows the orchestrator dispatches from this activity (via dispatch_child with an explicit workflow_id); the server does not act on trigger declarations.

outcome.description: Expected outcomes when activity completes successfully. Advisory — the server does not reconcile them against activity_manifest outcomes.

required.description: Whether this activity is required in the workflow

rules.description: Activity-level rules and constraints that agents must follow

artifactPrefix.description: Numeric prefix for artifact filenames, inferred from the activity filename (e.g., "02" from 02-design-philosophy.yaml). Server-computed — do not set in definition files.
